title: Retrying failed webhooks with backoff
summary: Webhook deliveries that fail are retried on a schedule that waits longer each time, and receivers can safely see the same event twice. The big idea: a retry is only safe when the receiver can tell it's a repeat.

concepts.name: Exponential backoff
concepts.explanation: Wait longer after each failure, doubling the delay every time (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s…). It gives a struggling server room to recover instead of hammering it with retries.
concepts.whyHere: Failed deliveries are rescheduled with delay = base × 2^attempt, capped at one hour.

concepts.name: Jitter
concepts.explanation: Add a random amount to each wait. Without it, every client that failed at the same moment retries at the same moment too.
concepts.whyHere: Each delay is randomized between 0 and the backoff value ("full jitter").

concepts.name: Idempotency keys
concepts.explanation: A unique ID sent with a request so the receiver can recognize a repeat and skip doing the work twice.
concepts.whyHere: Every delivery carries an Idempotency-Key header equal to the event ID, so retries can't double-charge.

concepts.name: Dead-letter queue
concepts.explanation: A holding area for messages that kept failing, so they stop retrying forever but aren't lost.
concepts.whyHere: After 8 attempts a delivery moves to the webhook_dead_letters table for manual replay.

concepts.name: HMAC signatures
concepts.explanation: A hash of the message made with a shared secret. The receiver recomputes it to prove the message came from you and wasn't changed.
concepts.whyHere: Each payload is signed with SHA-256 HMAC and a timestamp so receivers can reject forged or replayed webhooks.
